column1: ",https://share.descript.com/view/M7ktDjS5XE4,C01_CH01_L01_introduction_to_lyzr_platform.mp4,Take a use case where we will build an agent which is backed by knowledge base. So the use case goes as follows. We have an employee handbook from Nova Bridge Technologies and this handbook contains details about the employee policies at Nova Bridge Technologies. Let see what all it contains. It contains different employment policies code and conduct ethics compensation and benefits leave and time off policies and various other policies related to employees. What we want to do is build an agent that will answer any query related to employee policies. This agent will be used by employees of this company and they will ask any question related to employee policy. If the answer lies in this particular document the agent should be able to answer that particular query. However if the answer is not present in this particular document it should say that I do not know the answer to your query. So let see how we can do that So we are going to build this agent and the knowledge base in the studio platform at studio.lyza.ai. So firstly we will create the knowledge base. Followed by that we will create the agent which will use this knowledge base. In order to create the knowledge base from the left navigation menu go to Knowledge Base and on the top right click on the New button and select Knowledge Base. We will create a basic knowledge base. However we do support graph-based knowledge base as well. Let give it a good name say Nova Bridge Employee Policies a description Knowledge base containing employee policies for Nova Bridge Technologies employees. And then select the vector store as per your choice and the text embedding model as per your choice. I will leave both of them as default and I create the knowledge base. Now in knowledge base we support multiple types of sources. These are all unstructured data present in the form of text. So we support adding files. The files could be of different formats .pdf .docx .txt. We also support adding websites. Whenever you add a website you can crawl the website to multiple subpages and all those web pages could be added as a knowledge base. Then we also support text and live source. Live source supports drives like SharePoint and Google Drive as well as website. column5: >Knowledge Bases act as the long-term memory and factual anchor for Lyzr Agents. When a query is received:
>1. Ingestion & Chunking: Documents are parsed into semantically coherent text chunks.
>2. Embedding & Vector Storage: Chunks are embedded and stored in vector stores.
>3. Contextual Retrieval: The retriever fetches the top-K relevant chunks to ground the LLM response.
>1. Create a Knowledge Base: In Agent Studio or SDK, select Create Knowledge Base.
>2. Upload Documents: Attach PDF files, CSVs, or connect live data connectors.
>3. Select Chunking & Parser Strategy: Choose between standard text chunking or layout-aware PDF parsing.
>4. Wire to Agent: Connect the Knowledge Base to your agent's knowledge property.

column3: >Layout-aware parsing ensures tables and structured headers maintain context.
>Grounding agents in verified Knowledge Bases eliminates model hallucinations.

You start by building a simple agent and then you realize how powerful agents are and you start building agents. Slowly you want memory for the agents then comes the rag then comes integration with multiple tools putting together the guardrails so that the agents can be safely deployed to production putting together the testing framework for the agent observability for the agent and soon you realize there are lots of different pieces that are just out of your control. And that is where Leizer is your friend. It is a one-stop shop for managing the complete agent life cycle At Lysa we help enterprises reimagine their complex workflows with agentic AI automation. Let see some of the examples as to how Lysa has helped clients. So we have multiple clients across the globe and our mission is to take the workloads from being people native to being agent native. So here is an example of how we have helped WTW put together a retirement advisory solution. Yet another example that we have is for Accenture where we have put together a corporate venture capital function for them and now they have Agentic OS running two hundred plus agents multiple functions and it has just made their life very easy Here is yet another example of how we have helped KPMG to put together their procurement lifecycle solutions Now that you already know that it can put together multiple different types of solutions let us see how the Laiza stack is put together. At the bottommost layer of the stack is the infrastructure layer. The infrastructure layer specifies where all Laiza can be deployed. It can be deployed on any of the cloud providers be it Azure AWS or GCP. It can also be deployed on on-prem solutions like bare metal virtual machines. On top of this infrastructure layer is the integration layer with multiple models and third-party tools. column1: ",https://share.descript.com/view/GobPzBquAVF,C02_CH01_L03_equip_model_tool_memory_knowledge.mp4,In the last video we created our support agent. It can hold a conversation but right now it running on the model general knowledge. It doesn know a single thing about Northwind. So in this video we going to equip it. We give it a brain our own knowledge a tool and memory. First the model. This is the agent brain the engine that does the reasoning. Laser gives you a whole range to choose from across different providers. I keeping the default here OpenAI GPT 5.4 Mini. It fast and inexpensive which is exactly what you want for a high-volume support agent. And you not locked in. If you ever need more reasoning power you swap the model right here without rebuilding anything else. Now the most important step: knowledge. Here the problem we solving. If I ask a plain model about Northwind warranty it will give me a confident specific answer. It will be completely made up. That is the fastest way to lose a customer trust. The fix is to ground the agent in our own documents. I click Add Knowledge Base create one called Northwind Help Docs and upload our actual support documentation: returns warranty and shipping policies. Laser ingests that and now it attached to the agent. Let prove it works. I ask what is the warranty policy for laptops at Northwind? And look at the answer. Northwind laptops include a one-year limited manufacturer warranty covering defects in materials workmanship and it does not cover accidental damage liquid damage et cetera. It even offers to share the extended warranty policy. Every bit of that came straight from our docs not from the model imagination. That is the difference grounding makes. Next a tool. Knowledge is what the agent knows. Tools are what it can do. I attaching a web search tool. Our docs cover the vast majority of questions but every so often a customer asks something that falls outside them. With search attached the agent can look beyond the docs when it genuinely needs to instead of guessing. It sits in the background and the agent decides when to reach for it. And finally memory which is already on by default. This is what lets the agent remember the conversation so a customer never has to repeat themselves. It the difference between a real conversation and starting a blank state every single message. So now we have a real agent a brain or knowledge a tool for the edge cases and memory. It genuinely useful. But useful and safe to ship are not the same thing. In the next video we add guardrails. I Felipe with Lieser. See you there

column1: ",https://share.descript.com/view/FOzm28nV9YM,C02_CH01_L04_what_agent_type_should_i_build.mp4,Lysr gives you a few different agent types and picking the right one is the most important decision you make. So let walk through them and more importantly when to use each. We already covered single agents in the last course. A single agent is the right call when one agent can handle the whole task on its own and that always where you start. The real question is when to move beyond a single agent and which way to go. And there is one guiding principle behind all of this. Choose the simplest architecture that can reliably solve your problem. You only reach for more when a single agent stops being reliable. The first step up is the manager agent. You reach for it when the problem is complex enough that one agent can reliably handle it and when the work is conversational and non-deterministic. That means ambiguity reasoning planning decision-making delegating tasks on the fly. Think of an AI consultant a research assistant or a customer support system that has to think through a few possibilities before it answers. Behind the scenes several specialized agents collaborate but to the user it one smooth conversation. The other direction is Superflow and it almost the opposite. Superflow is for deterministic automation. Instead of letting agents decide what happens next you define the workflow explicitly. It ideal for one-shot business processes where the sequence is known in advance: employee onboarding payment processing patient intake or resume screening document processing and approval workflows. Anywhere you want the system to behave the same way every time with no surprises. Superflow gives you that predictability through structured orchestration. Then there voice. Voice agents aren really a different brain they a different way in. The intelligence underneath can still be a single agent a manager or Superflow. Voice just lets people talk to it instead of type. You use it when speaking is the natural interaction: customer support healthcare intake appointment scheduling field operation sales and contract centers. So here how to choose. A single agent when one agent can solve the problem on its own a manager agent when it needs reasoning collaboration planning or handling ambiguity a Superflow when the process is deterministic and follows a defined sequence of steps and voice when the main way people interact is by speaking. Start simple and move up only when you have to. Step up to a manager when you need intelligence and collaboration and reach for Superflow when predictability and process control matter more than dynamic reasoning. Over the next few videos we build each of these for real

column1: ",https://share.descript.com/view/JxjoIomKT1C,C02_CH02_L01_lyzr_manager_orchestration.mp4,A single agent is great right up until the question has two jobs buried in it. My order isn here and I want to return something. That really two requests. Instead of building one giant agent that tries to do everything you build a team and put a manager in charge. Let me show you. From the home screen I open Orchestrate and go into the manager. This canvas is where you compose a team of agents. I search our agents and here the team we use: a support agent that knows our policies an order lookup agent and a returns agent. I drop the support agent on first then add the other two. Each one is good at exactly one thing. Now the key move: I connect the support agent to the other two. That connection is what turns it into a manager. Watch the badge. Support is now the manager and order lookup and returns are its sub-agents. And notice I never specified an order to call them in. The manager decides that itself. column1: ",https://share.descript.com/view/e9Ny8ysXwMc,C02_CH02_L02_superflow_basic_dynamic_flows.mp4,Real agentic work is almost never one agent answering one prompt. It several steps. This workflow is called invoice reconciliation. The story is simple. An invoice comes in we parse it we pull out the invoice ID and the total amount. We check the ID against our system of record. If it matches the file goes straight to S3. If it doesn the workflow pauses. An agent writes a summary for the human approver. Extract fields runs an extraction model against that parsed text using a schema I defined. I asking for two things: an invoice ID and a total amount. column1: ",https://share.descript.com/view/CGqBLgAbGUG,C02_CH03_L03_document_parsing_ingestion.mp4,When you drop a document into a knowledge base a lot happens before your agent can use it and the quality of that process quietly decides how good your answers are. So let look at what ingestion actually does the one knob that matters most and how to keep your knowledge from going stale. Here the knowledge base we built. When I added these documents Lysr didn just store them. It read each one pulled the text out of it split it into chunks and turned every chunk into an embedding a numerical fingerprint it can search against. That ingestion. And here the thing to internalize: garbage in garbage out. A clean document ingests beautifully. A messy scanned PDF is harder to parse and if the text comes out garbled no clever prompting will save your answers. So the quality of your source documents matters more than almost anything else. Now the one knob worth knowing. Let me run a query first so you can see the raw retrieval. I search warranty and I get three matches: the top one from our product guide at about eighty-three percent then our support docs at seventy-nine and another chunk at seventy-one. Three results with different confidence scores. Sometimes you don want every loosely related chunk. You only want the strong matches. That the score threshold. Under Configure I set it to zero point eight which means only matches above eighty percent confidence come back. Then I hit Save Same query again and now I get exactly one result the product guide at 83%. The 79 and 71% matches got filtered out because they didn clear the bar I set. That the trade. Lower the threshold when you want the agent to see more context. Raise it when you only want high confidence answers. This one setting does a lot of the work in tuning answer quality One last piece and it what keeps your agent from going stale. Every knowledge base has an API so you don have to babysit it. You can update it from your own systems automatically. My favorite example is a support team. Every time a ticket gets resolved you push that resolution into the knowledge base through this API. The next customer with the same problem gets the answer instantly because your agent just learned it here the config and here the inference endpoint you call. Your knowledge base stays current without anyone uploading a thing. So that ingestion and retrieval. Get clean documents in use the score threshold to dial in precision and use the API to keep it fresh. Next we look at connecting external data sources. I am Felipe Wollizer. I see you there

column1: ",https://share.descript.com/view/zMdeiKC7LUO,C02_CH04_L01_agent_memory_in_depth.mp4,Your agent has a brain. Now let give it a memory. Without one every conversation starts from a blank slate and your customer has to reintroduce themselves every time. With it the agent remembers. The interesting part isn switching it on. It deciding what counts as the same conversation and what counts as the same person. Memory is a feature you turn on. Under Features I open the full list switch on Memory and that opens its settings. First choice is the provider. Lyzr gives you a few but the default is Cognis and for almost everyone that the answer. It production-grade memory and you really don need to touch it. I leave it on Cognis. Now the setting that actually matters and the one people get wrong: cross-session. To understand it you need two ideas. A session is one conversation. A user is one person who might have many conversations over time. By default memory lives inside a single session so a brand-new chat starts clean. Turn cross-session on and memory follows the person across all their conversations. I turning it on and in a second you see exactly what that changes There also an extraction instructions tab where you can steer what the agent bothers to remember. The default is fine so I leave it. I save that and update the agent Now let test it. In the playground I tell it something personal my name and that I prefer email updates It acknowledges and quietly stores that for later. Here the proof. I start a completely new chat. Normally that a clean slate a different session no memory of the last one. But watch. I ask who I am and how I like to be contacted and it answers Your name is Felipe and you prefer to receive updates by email. Brand-new session and it still knows me. That cross-session memory. It remembered the person not just the conversation. And here what that looks like when you wire it into your own product which is where this gets slightly technical. On the Deploy tab you got the agent API. When you call it you pass the agent ID and a session ID. The same session ID continues a conversation. A new one starts fresh. That how you control what a conversation means out in the real world. And because we turned on cross-session the agent ties memory to the person behind those sessions so a returning customer is recognized instead of starting over. You manage the sessions Lyzr handles the memory Turn it on keep cog-- Turn it on keep cognisis as the provider and the real decision is scope. A normal
